2026-09-15 lesson (hel-oj1 rounds 4 to 7): proving a worktree HEAD is the verified commit rebased. No diff comparison works. git patch-id --stable strips whitespace; --verbatim ignores bytes after a NUL and mode lines; git show output bends to git config (diff.submodule=log splits the patch, ignoreSubmodules=all hides pointer changes). A SHA-256 over pinned-flag git show bytes fixes those but stays position-blind once hunk headers are normalized away, so an edit moved to an identical block compares equal. Replay instead of compare, and replay commit by commit: a single squashed git merge-tree of the whole range loses per-commit rename detection, so a branch that renames a file then rewrites it while main edits the old path rebases cleanly yet replays as a modify/delete conflict, and helios then refuses the HEAD it rebased itself on every rerun. Final rule: cursor starts at merge-base(HEAD, main); for each commit c of output_base..output_commit run git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<c^> <cursor> <c>, exit 1 refuses, then cursor = commit-tree of the replayed tree; the final cursor tree must equal HEAD's tree. A missing or empty merge-base refuses (exit 2), and every git call takes --no-replace-objects. Probes: tmp/fp-probe, tmp/replay-probe, tmp/seq-probe. Probe an equivalence rule against position, renames across commits, config, NUL, mode and submodule variants before writing it into the SPEC.

2026-09-16 Claude Code background jobs: the orchestrator cannot edit the shared checkout at all. Edit and Write against the hub are refused until the session isolates, and the refusal names EnterWorktree. But once the session is isolated by EnterWorktree, every git command is refused too, including read-only ones such as git status, because the rtk rewrite hides which git runs and the worktree guard will not allow a git it cannot attribute. Those two rules together mean neither the hub nor an isolated session can both edit and commit.

The pattern that works, in this order: create the worktree from the hub with plain git, git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<id> -b worktree-<id> followed by git worktree lock --reason keep; call EnterWorktree with the path, never with a name; make every edit; call ExitWorktree with action keep, which returns the session to the hub and leaves the branch and directory intact; then commit and merge from the hub, where git works normally. Writing the commit message to a file outside the repository and using git commit -F avoids quoting problems with multi-line messages.

This cost six refused edits and four refused git calls before it was understood. Subagents are unaffected: they never call EnterWorktree, so they edit and commit inside their worktree normally.

Configuration refusals and telemetry span order in helios, closing hel-f1g, hel-xev and hel-5eh.

config.ConfigError lives in src/helios/config.py and subclasses ValueError. load() validates in _load_file and wraps every TypeError or ValueError from it in ConfigError, so no caller has to know which builtin a given check raises. cli.main() holds the one handler that prints 'helios: <message>' and returns 2; the ten command modules with their own handler catch ConfigError first through ValueError and print the identical line, so they never reach the shared handler. Do not add a copy of that handler to a new command module: loading configuration outside a handler is now correct, because cli.main covers it. Loader tests in tests/test_config.py expect config.ConfigError, not TypeError; all eleven such sites went through cfg.load.

tests/test_templates.py loads templates/workflow.toml through the real loader and compares field by field with Config(hub). The harness dict is compared per entry rather than against default.harness, because a bare Config names no harness while the template names claude, codex, opencode and agy as empty tables. A guard test damages the template two ways and asserts each is refused. Damage the template by replacing a line, never by appending a table, since appending duplicates an existing table and raises a TOML parse error instead of the unknown key or wrong type the test claims to check.

SPEC section 21 lists the attempt children as launch, validate, check.<name>, commit. That is the order of section 7.1, which parses and classifies at step 8, runs the checks at step 9 and commits at step 10, so the emitted order agrees with the span timestamps. _attempt_trace in src/helios/run.py builds them in that order and tests/test_telemetry.py asserts both the names and that the start timestamps rise with them. A failed or skipped merge export is silent by specification: a merge has no attempt record, helios merge has a fixed stderr and exit code contract from section 12, and its bead comments are the step markers the replay rule of section 7.5 reads back, so neither can carry a telemetry note.

The full suite is slow: 1283 tests, about 10 minutes 35 seconds. Run it in the background and wait on the summary line, never in the foreground with a 120 second tool timeout.
